evidence.note: Binary 40MB cap and job-queue BEGIN IMMEDIATE/retry/dead-letter claim semantics are set up as first-class planned constraints (framework selection tied to size; jobs task explicitly names claim contract).
Binary size checked after build and again at final cleanup — the size constraint is verified more than once, i.e. actively tracked not just planned.
Explicit process-tree check confirming no Ruby runtime in the service tree — direct guarding of the no-Ruby prohibition.
Reference server started side-by-side purely for differential comparison, not proxied; only the shared DB is used cross-runtime, consistent with the no-TCP-to-reference rule.
Jobs.rs/db.rs iterated on claim semantics (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, retry/backoff), treating shared-DB interop as a matched contract rather than an afterthought.

reasoning: The agent actively guarded most hard constraints — repeatedly checking binary size, auditing the process tree for Ruby, using the reference only for comparison, and treating BEGIN IMMEDIATE claim semantics as a contract — which places it above the level-5 'verify obvious ones once' anchor and near level 8. It falls short of 10 because latency parity was never measured as a ratio, the Cargo.toml bridge-crate check isn't explicit, and the checks cluster toward the end rather than functioning as standing gates re-run throughout the loop.
